questions.title: Permeability of membrane models
questions.stem:
Vesicles of equal surface area contain solute X. Values are initial outward fluxes at the same temperature and the same starting X gradient. Channel Z conducts X when open. The inhibitor is proposed to block Z.

| Membrane | Inhibitor | Flux / arbitrary units |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lipid only | Absent | 2 |
| Lipid only | Present | 2 |
| Lipid + Z | Absent | 18 |
| Lipid + Z | Present | 6 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the fraction of channel-associated flux removed by the inhibitor, correcting for the lipid-only background.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why the results support facilitated diffusion and do not establish active transport.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State why the lipid-only inhibitor control is needed and suggest one further measurement of selectivity.

steps.text: Without inhibitor the channel-associated flux is 18−2=16 and with inhibitor it is 6−2=4.
Fraction removed=(16−4)/16=0.75 or 75%.
An open protein increases flux in the direction of the existing gradient.
There is no evidence of uphill movement driven by an energy source.
It tests whether inhibitor alters background permeability independent of Z.
Measure flux of a second solute through the same membranes under matched gradients.

questions.answerSummary: Without inhibitor the channel-associated flux is 18−2=16 and with inhibitor it is 6−2=4.

questions.title: Two exposures to an antigen
questions.stem:
An individual receives a first dose of antigen on day 0 and a booster on day 28. Antibody values are in arbitrary units. Samples were collected at the times shown.

| Day | 0 | 7 | 14 | 28 | 35 | 42 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antibody | 1 | 4 | 32 | 8 | 80 | 128 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Compare antibody concentration seven days after each exposure using a ratio.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain the biological basis for the faster secondary response.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Evaluate the claim that these measurements prove the booster prevents disease in all recipients.

steps.text: Compare day 7 with day 35.
80/4=20, so the measured concentration seven days after the booster is twenty times as high.
Specific memory cells persist after the primary response.
They rapidly proliferate and form antibody-secreting cells after re-exposure to the antigen.
Antibody concentration is an immune marker and the data come from one person.
Protection requires evidence such as infection or disease outcomes in suitable comparison groups across recipients.

questions.title: Counting dividing cells
questions.stem:
At one instant, observers classified cells in two root-tip regions. They used the same rules and counted complete fields. The mitotic index is the fraction of cells observed in mitosis.

| Region | Interphase | Prophase | Metaphase | Anaphase | Telophase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | 144 | 18 | 8 | 4 | 6 |
| Q | 171 | 9 | 5 | 2 | 3 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the mitotic index in each region.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A student says P must have a cell cycle half as long as Q. Evaluate this inference.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Describe a way to test inter-observer reliability without counting different fields.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Give a visible criterion distinguishing anaphase from metaphase.

steps.text: P has 36 mitotic cells out of 180, giving 0.200.
Q has 19 out of 190, giving 0.100.
P has twice the observed fraction in mitosis.
The fraction also depends on mitotic duration and on the proportion of actively cycling cells, so it does not alone give cycle length.
Give both observers the same anonymized images and have them classify independently.
Compare their classifications or agreement for individual cells using predefined criteria.
In anaphase two sets of chromatids move toward opposite poles instead of being aligned at the equator.
